subject: Warm seed wave + query failover orchestration for Brightline Health
messages:

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Warm seed wave + query failover orchestration for Brightline Health

Emma —

Thanks again for the sync today. Per our conversation I put together a concise plan for the warm-seed wave and the query failover that will accompany the rerank cutover. The goal is to:

- Seed the vector index with prioritized content (Q4 product docs + top 50k support articles).
- Run rerank evaluation with a held-out set of 1,500 queries and produce precision@10 / MRR snapshots.
- Keep query traffic live during the backfill using a read-through failover to the old BM25 index for any missing IDs.

High level schedule proposal (please confirm):
- Preflight & access: Dec 2–3 (service account + S3 bucket access)
- Warm seed: Dec 4–6 (staggered batches at night to limit write pressure)
- Validation & rerank smoke: Dec 7
- Cutover window (gradual shift + monitoring): Dec 8, 10:00–13:00 PT

Immediate asks for Brightline team:
1) Provide an S3 path or temporary transfer for the seed payloads (CSV/JSONL) and a service account with write to your staging vector DB.
2) Confirm whether you prefer our Milvus-managed cluster (recommended for large bulk writes) or Pinecone for lower operational overhead after cutover.
3) Security contacts for SOC/audit evidence if needed during the window.

I've attached a short workbook (brightline_warm_seed_plan_v1.xlsx) that breaks the batches into 12 shards and includes rollback checkpoints.

If those dates look okay I'll put together the canary traffic plan and invite the right ops contacts.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks, this looks reasonable. Dec 2–3 for preflight is OK, Dec 8 cutover window works for our product team. A couple of quick clarifications before we lock it:

- Vector DB: Our platform team historically used FAISS on VMs for local dev, but for production we're open to your recommendation. Is Milvus significantly better for a 120M vector corpus?
- Failover semantics: when a query falls back to BM25, do you preserve rerank scoring later (i.e., will those follow-up queries be re-evaluated once the item exists in the vector index)?
- PII: some seed docs contain limited PHI. We'll need confirmation on in-flight encryption and logging scope.

I'll loop in our eng lead (cc'd) and procurement for SOW scheduling.

Emma Lawson

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@brightline.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T08:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Warm seed wave + query failover orchestration for Brightline Health

Emma — thanks for the questions — answers inline: 

1) Vector DB choice: For a 120M vector corpus Milvus (managed by us) reduces write contention with partitioned shards and streaming bulk imports; it also supports chunked imports and parallel ingestion. Pinecone is simpler but will need a strategy for large bulk imports (we do staged warm writes into a temporary namespace and then alias). FAISS is great for on-prem or single-node inference but becomes operationally heavy at this scale. Our recommendation: Milvus-managed for the initial large seed, then evaluate moving read traffic to Pinecone aliases if you want lower ops surface.

2) Failover semantics: Our read-through layer will return BM25 results for missing vector IDs. We keep a short-lived request cache and a reconciliation job that replays recent queries through the vector index post-seed. So user sessions that hit BM25 will not be re-ranked retroactively, but follow-up identical queries from the same user will benefit once the item is present. We can extend session-based re-querying if that's important — that would require a front-end hook for re-ranking on next user request.

3) PII: All data in transit will be TLS 1.3. Seed payloads should be s3:// path with SSE-KMS enabled; we will not persist raw seed files beyond the seeding job unless explicitly requested. Audit logs for the seeding process can be exported to your KMS-protected bucket. Ben, can you confirm the default retention for seeding logs and whether we can mask identifiers on export?

Next steps:
- Ben will share the backfill script and the ops runbook.
- Monica will coordinate the cutover play call invite list.

If that sounds good I'll produce a terse canary checklist and invite a cutover rehearsal on Dec 4.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Lawson <emma@brightline.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T07:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Warm seed wave + query failover orchestration for Brightline Health

Hi all —

Attaching the lightweight backfill runner and a short checklist. Key technical notes: 

- backfill-script.sh (attached stub) runs in 12 parallel workers, verifies MD5 per shard and writes a success marker file to s3://brightline-seed/markers/<shard>. Success marker triggers the reconciliation consumer to index the shard.
- During warm seed we will: 1) throttle to 1250 writes/sec per shard; 2) emit per-shard telemetry (write latency, 4xx/5xx rates); 3) create read-only alias once shard complete.
- Rollback: if a shard fails more than 3 times we will mark it failed and skip; operations will backfill with a lower pressure wave the next night.

Security: script uses short-lived STS tokens and writes nothing to disk on the runner. Logs can be streamed to your KMS bucket; by default we redact user identifiers in the first-pass logs. If you need full-detail logs for audit, we can enable that behind a separate export with an approval step.

I'll include a short smoke-test set (rerank-eval-set.csv) — please keep that file in the staging path; we use it for pre/post precision checks.

Ben
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma —

I'll run the cutover playbook and own the go/no-go checklist. Minimum acceptance criteria we will validate during the canary and full roll: 

- Index parity: sample of 10K documents must have vector fingerprints that match expected hashes (zero mismatches allowed in canary).
- Rerank quality: precision@10 >= baseline + 7% (we'll run the rerank-eval-set.csv pre/post).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference time for the reranker must be <= 220ms.
- Ops: no more than 0.5% 5xx or error spike sustained over 10 minutes during warm seed.

On the cutover call please include: Brightline eng (lead), SRE, Redwood infra (Ben), Redwood CSM (me), and product owner. I will put the calendar invite for the rehearsal on Dec 4 09:00 PT and the live cutover on Dec 8 10:00 PT.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Procurement confirmed the SOW and we've provisioned a staging S3 path: s3://brightline-staging/seed-q4 (SSE-KMS enabled). Engineering will create a short-lived service account and drop the key in your secure link by EOD Dec 1.

Two small asks before rehearsal: 
- Can the redwood backfill job add an optional "mask_user_ids" flag? We prefer to scrub user identifiers in first-pass logs.
- We'll also want an explicit confirmation in the operations report that seed payloads are not retained longer than 7 days by default.

If those are OK we'll join the Dec 4 rehearsal. See you then.

Emma
